# Control API reference

<!-- Generated by `cargo test -p hiccup-control`: edit crates/hiccup-control/src/api.rs, then run it with HICCUP_BLESS=1. -->

API version **1.0**. Hiccup instances (`hiccup serve`, `hiccup proxy start --foreground`, the desktop apps) accept [JSON-RPC 2.0](https://www.jsonrpc.org/specification) requests, one JSON object per line, on a local socket: a Unix domain socket (mode `0600`, in a `0700` directory) on Linux and macOS, and a named pipe restricted to the current user on Windows. See [ADR 0004](adr/0004-cli-control-plane.md).

Instances register in the per-user runtime directory (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hiccup` on Linux, `hiccup/run` in the local data directory elsewhere): `<name>.json` gives the instance's endpoint. The directory must be private to the user: on Unix, clients refuse one that other users can access, as they could plant records pointing to their own endpoints.

Clients call `instance.info` first and refuse an instance whose major `api_version` differs. Minor versions only add methods, fields and notifications.

Errors use the JSON-RPC codes (-32700 parse error, -32600 invalid request, -32601 unknown method, -32602 invalid parameters, -32603 internal error) and Hiccup's: -32000 the operation failed, -32001 it conflicts with the current state.

## Methods

### `instance.info`

Describe the instance. Clients call it first to check `api_version`.

Parameters:

```json
{}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "api_version": "1.0",
  "name": "default",
  "pid": 4242,
  "project": "/home/me/work/acme.hiccup",
  "started_at": 1790000000,
  "version": "0.1.0"
}
```

### `instance.shutdown`

Stop the instance, and its proxy. Connected clients first get an `instance.stopping` notification.

Parameters:

```json
{}
```

Result:

```json
{}
```

### `proxy.start`

Start the proxy with TLS interception, loading the CA (or generating it on first use). Every parameter is optional; paths must be absolute.

Parameters:

```json
{
  "client_certs": [
    {
      "cert": "/home/me/client.pem",
      "host": "*.corp.test"
    }
  ],
  "listen": [
    "127.0.0.1:8080"
  ],
  "read_timeout_ms": 30000,
  "resolve": [
    {
      "host": "app.test",
      "value": "10.0.0.5"
    }
  ],
  "tls_passthrough": [
    "*.mozilla.com"
  ],
  "upstream_sni": [],
  "verify_upstream": true
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "ca_generated": false,
  "ca_sha256": "B3:F7:03:…:92:43",
  "proxy": {
    "exchanges": 0,
    "listen": [
      "127.0.0.1:8080"
    ],
    "running": true,
    "verify_upstream": true
  }
}
```

Errors:

- `-32602`: a parameter is invalid (address, pattern, TLS version, file)
- `-32001`: the proxy is already running
- `-32000`: an address cannot be bound, or the CA cannot be loaded

### `proxy.stop`

Stop the proxy. In-flight exchanges get a short grace period.

Parameters:

```json
{}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "exchanges": 0,
  "listen": [],
  "running": false,
  "verify_upstream": false
}
```

Errors:

- `-32001`: the proxy is not running

### `proxy.status`

Describe the proxy.

Parameters:

```json
{}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "exchanges": 42,
  "listen": [
    "127.0.0.1:8080"
  ],
  "running": true,
  "verify_upstream": true
}
```

### `intercept.status`

Describe the intercept settings. They belong to the instance and apply to its proxy whenever it runs.

Parameters:

```json
{}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "pending": 1,
  "requests": {
    "hosts": [
      "*.example.com"
    ],
    "in_scope": true,
    "methods": [
      "POST"
    ],
    "path": "^/api/"
  },
  "responses": null
}
```

### `intercept.set`

Replace the intercept settings. Items held in a direction that is turned off are forwarded unchanged.

Parameters:

```json
{
  "requests": {
    "hosts": [
      "*.example.com"
    ],
    "in_scope": true,
    "methods": [
      "POST"
    ],
    "path": "^/api/"
  },
  "responses": null
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "pending": 1,
  "requests": {
    "hosts": [
      "*.example.com"
    ],
    "in_scope": true,
    "methods": [
      "POST"
    ],
    "path": "^/api/"
  },
  "responses": null
}
```

Errors:

- `-32602`: a host pattern, regular expression or timeout is invalid

### `intercept.list`

List the held items, oldest first.

Parameters:

```json
{}
```

Result:

```json
[
  {
    "age_ms": 1500,
    "direction": "request",
    "id": 7,
    "method": "POST",
    "size": 412,
    "target": "/api/login",
    "tls": true,
    "upstream": "example.com:443"
  }
]
```

### `intercept.show`

Show one held item with the exact bytes that would be sent.

Parameters:

```json
{
  "id": 7
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "age_ms": 1500,
  "direction": "request",
  "id": 7,
  "method": "POST",
  "raw": "UE9TVCAvYXBpL2xvZ2luIEhUVFAvMS4xDQo…",
  "size": 412,
  "target": "/api/login",
  "tls": true,
  "upstream": "example.com:443"
}
```

Errors:

- `-32001`: no held item has this ID (resolved or timed out)

### `intercept.forward`

Forward a held item. With `raw`, those bytes are sent instead, exactly as given; an edited response closes the client connection after it.

Parameters:

```json
{
  "id": 7,
  "raw": "UE9TVCAvYXBpL2xvZ2luIEhUVFAvMS4xDQo…"
}
```

Result:

```json
{}
```

Errors:

- `-32001`: no held item has this ID (resolved or timed out)
- `-32602`: `raw` is not valid base64

### `intercept.drop`

Drop a held item. The client gets a 502 response from Hiccup.

Parameters:

```json
{
  "id": 7
}
```

Result:

```json
{}
```

Errors:

- `-32001`: no held item has this ID (resolved or timed out)

### `intercept.forward_all`

Forward every held item unchanged.

Parameters:

```json
{}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "forwarded": 3
}
```

### `events.subscribe`

Receive events on this connection, as notifications, until it closes. Events are buffered: a subscriber that falls too far behind gets `events.lagged`, then the connection closes; reconnect and subscribe again (state such as held items can be listed afresh).

Parameters:

```json
{}
```

Result:

```json
{}
```

### `history.list`

List recorded exchanges, newest first. History is recorded when the instance has a project (`hiccup serve --project FILE`).

Parameters:

```json
{
  "host": "example.com",
  "limit": 50,
  "status": 200
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "client": "127.0.0.1:52344",
      "duration_ms": 87,
      "id": 42,
      "method": "GET",
      "mime": "application/json",
      "request_size": 412,
      "response_size": 5321,
      "started_ms": 1764000000000,
      "status": 200,
      "target": "/api/items?page=2",
      "tls": true,
      "upstream": "example.com:443"
    }
  ]
}
```

Errors:

- `-32001`: no project is open (start the instance with --project)
- `-32602`: `limit` is above 1000

### `history.show`

Show one recorded exchange with its exact bytes.

Parameters:

```json
{
  "id": 42
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "client": "127.0.0.1:52344",
  "duration_ms": 87,
  "forwarded": "R0VUIC9hcGkvaXRlbXM/cGFnZT0yIEhUVFAvMS4xDQo…",
  "id": 42,
  "method": "GET",
  "mime": "application/json",
  "received": "R0VUIC9hcGkvaXRlbXM/cGFnZT0yIEhUVFAvMS4xDQo…",
  "request_size": 412,
  "response": "SFRUUC8xLjEgMjAwIE9LDQo…",
  "response_size": 5321,
  "started_ms": 1764000000000,
  "status": 200,
  "target": "/api/items?page=2",
  "tls": true,
  "upstream": "example.com:443"
}
```

Errors:

- `-32001`: no project is open (start the instance with --project)
- `-32602`: no recorded exchange has this ID

### `scope.list`

List the scope rules. They belong to the instance; intercept rules with `in_scope` use them.

Parameters:

```json
{}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "rules": [
    {
      "host": "*.example.com",
      "protocol": "https"
    },
    {
      "exclude": true,
      "path": "^/logout"
    }
  ]
}
```

### `scope.add`

Add a scope rule at the end. Returns every rule.

Parameters:

```json
{
  "host": "*.example.com",
  "protocol": "https"
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "rules": [
    {
      "host": "*.example.com",
      "protocol": "https"
    },
    {
      "exclude": true,
      "path": "^/logout"
    }
  ]
}
```

Errors:

- `-32602`: the protocol, host pattern or regular expression is invalid

### `scope.remove`

Remove a scope rule. Returns the remaining rules.

Parameters:

```json
{
  "index": 1
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "rules": [
    {
      "host": "*.example.com",
      "protocol": "https"
    }
  ]
}
```

Errors:

- `-32602`: no rule has this index

### `scope.test`

Tell whether a URL is in scope.

Parameters:

```json
{
  "url": "https://app.example.com/login"
}
```

Result:

```json
{
  "in_scope": true
}
```

Errors:

- `-32602`: the URL is not an `http://` or `https://` URL

## Notifications

### `instance.stopping`

The instance is stopping; the connection will close. Sent to every connection.

Parameters:

```json
{}
```

### `exchange.request`

A request was received, before it is held or forwarded. Events from here on are sent after `events.subscribe` only.

Parameters:

```json
{
  "id": 12,
  "method": "GET",
  "target": "/api/items?page=2",
  "tls": true,
  "upstream": "example.com:443"
}
```

### `exchange.response`

An exchange completed (its response was relayed in full), or failed.

Parameters:

```json
{
  "duration_ms": 87,
  "id": 12,
  "size": 5321,
  "status": 200
}
```

### `intercept.pending`

A message is held in the intercept queue (as in `intercept.list`).

Parameters:

```json
{
  "age_ms": 1500,
  "direction": "request",
  "id": 7,
  "method": "POST",
  "size": 412,
  "target": "/api/login",
  "tls": true,
  "upstream": "example.com:443"
}
```

### `intercept.resolved`

A held message left the intercept queue.

Parameters:

```json
{
  "id": 7,
  "outcome": "edited"
}
```

### `proxy.state`

The proxy started or stopped (as in `proxy.status`).

Parameters:

```json
{
  "exchanges": 42,
  "listen": [
    "127.0.0.1:8080"
  ],
  "running": true,
  "verify_upstream": true
}
```

### `events.lagged`

The subscriber fell behind and missed events; the connection closes next.

Parameters:

```json
{
  "missed": 42
}
```
